feedback.problem: Let $f$ be a function with $f(2)=3,{f}^{′}(2)=2,{f}^{″}(2)=-4$ and ${f}^{‴}(2)=6.$ Which of the following is the third-degree Taylor polynomial for $f$ about $x=2?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =f(2)+{f}^{′}(2)(x-2)+\frac{{f}^{″}(2)}{2!}(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(2)}{3!}(x-2)^{3} \\  & =f(2)+{f}^{′}(2)(x-2)+\frac{{f}^{″}(2)}{2}(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(2)}{6}(x-2)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We have been given the following set of values: 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) & =3 \\ {f}^{′}(2) & =2 \\ {f}^{″}(2) & =-4 \\ {f}^{‴}(2) & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given values into our Taylor polynomial, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =3+2(x-2)+\frac{-4}{2}(x-2)^{2}+\frac{6}{6}(x-2)^{3} \\  & =3+2(x-2)-2(x-2)^{2}+(x-2)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
